brief: Yesterday's AI-complex squeeze did not fix the underlying problem: former darlings remain under heavy selling and valuation compression across the AI chain is extreme. Bernstein's 66-stock, nine-sector study finds data center exposure explains ~45% of that compression; memory and server OEMs are hit hardest, networking held up better, so the market is turning selective. SNDK trades at 2.5x forward earnings versus a 10.4x three-year average, nearly double the compression Bernstein's exposure model implies, though its true exposure may be higher; it is oversold since October, down over half, nearing a bearish 50-day/200-day cross. But new customer deals lock in roughly half of FY27 and two-thirds of FY28 bit volumes, and Bernstein estimates high-bandwidth flash at 5% of NAND demand would need ~28% more wafers, suggesting the market overweights future supply versus demand, making SNDK almost a contrarian trade. Bernstein also prefers STX among cheap HDD names on an early pricing upcycle. CRWV stays under-punished: the risk is funding contracted demand, not demand itself. NBIS's bounce failed to hold, leaving $80 as key support. AVGO is Bernstein's top semiconductor pick for its better-capitalized AI customer base. CIEN could gain from AI infrastructure's power and land constraints, via distributed data-center networking.
